prompt: How many keys are on a standard piano?
reveal: 88 keys: 52 white and 36 black, spanning just over seven octaves. Older pianos were built with 85 or fewer.

prompt: How many strings does a standard violin have?
reveal: Four strings — G, D, A and E — tuned in fifths. Fewer strings than a guitar, but a far wider expressive range in trained hands.

prompt: How many strings does a standard acoustic guitar have?
reveal: Six, tuned E–A–D–G–B–E. Twelve-string guitars double them in pairs, with the lower four pairs tuned in octaves.

prompt: How many players from one team are on a football (soccer) pitch at a time?
reveal: Eleven per side including the goalkeeper. Law 3 of the Laws of the Game fixes the number; a match cannot start with fewer than seven.

prompt: How many squares are on a standard chessboard?
reveal: 64 squares in an 8×8 grid, 32 light and 32 dark. A full set of move sequences is measured in the tens of billions of possibilities after only a few moves.

prompt: How many players from one team are on a basketball court at a time?
reveal: Five per team. The sport is built around that number: with ten players on a much smaller floor than football, spacing is everything.

prompt: How many rings are on the Olympic flag?
reveal: Five interlocking rings on a white field, representing the five inhabited continents that took part when Pierre de Coubertin designed it in 1913.

prompt: How many Olympic gold medals did swimmer Michael Phelps win?
reveal: 23 golds across four Games, plus 3 silver and 2 bronze — 28 medals in total, more than any other Olympian.

prompt: How many minutes are in one day?
reveal: 24 × 60 = 1,440 minutes. A useful anchor: 1,000 minutes is a bit under 17 hours, and a million seconds is only about 11.6 days.

prompt: How many days are in a leap year?
reveal: 366 — one extra day in February. Leap years keep the calendar aligned with Earth's 365.25-day orbit; century years skip the leap day unless divisible by 400.

prompt: How many member states are in the United Nations?
reveal: 193 member states, plus two permanent observer states. South Sudan was the most recent addition, in 2011.

prompt: How many people live in the Tokyo metropolitan area?
reveal: About 37 million people — the largest urban agglomeration on Earth, and more than the entire population of Canada.

prompt: How many moons does Mars have?
reveal: Two: Phobos and Deimos. Both are tiny, irregular lumps — probably captured asteroids — and Phobos is slowly spiralling in toward the planet.

prompt: What is the average distance from Earth to the Sun?
reveal: About 149.6 million km — one astronomical unit, now fixed by definition at exactly 149,597,870.7 km. Sunlight covers it in about 8 minutes 20 seconds.

prompt: How many teeth does a typical adult human have?
reveal: 32 including the four wisdom teeth — 16 upper and 16 lower. Most adults lose or have the wisdom teeth removed, leaving 28.

prompt: How many chambers does the human heart have?
reveal: Four: two atria that receive blood and two ventricles that pump it. The left ventricle does the heavy lifting, driving blood through the whole body.

prompt: How many chromosomes are in a typical human cell?
reveal: 46 chromosomes in 23 pairs — one of each pair from each parent. Sex cells carry 23; a fertilised egg restores the full set.

prompt: How many bones are in the adult human foot?
reveal: 26 bones per foot — over a quarter of all the bones in the body. Babies start with more; several fuse during childhood.

prompt: How fast can a cheetah run at full sprint?
reveal: Around 100 km/h over short bursts — the fastest land animal. It can only hold that for a few hundred metres before overheating.

prompt: How tall is the Burj Khalifa?
reveal: 828 m — more than 160 storeys, and the tallest structure ever built. Its own weight required changes mid-construction because the original design was unstable at that height.

prompt: How long is the Great Wall of China, measured end to end?
reveal: About 21,196 km counting every branch and the trenches and natural barriers — the single-line main wall is roughly 8,850 km.

prompt: How many lines are in a Shakespearean sonnet?
reveal: 14 lines in three quatrains plus a couplet, rhymed abab cdcd efef gg. The turn — the argument's reversal — usually lands at line 9 or 13.
